result.lens: YouTube retention strategist (documentary channels). Inputs: script plus word timings, the pacing table, all 9 contact sheets, the temporal scan, and about 30 frame-exact grab.py checks of every pop, flash and seam cluster. Predicted average view duration (AVD) is about 35% (about 5:57 of 16:51), 0:30 at 68%, 1:00 at 59%. The user said the animation was broken in places, so every rendering or animation fault is prefixed 'ANIMATION DEFECT' with frame-exact times.
result.would_leave_at: 14:04 (844 s). This is where "So is the drip just a coincidence?" starts the recap. I got the answer at 11:32 and the Holden twist at 12:38, then sat through 70 s of exceptions on near-still pictures (Baja, Florida limestone, Agulhas). The recap sounds like the ending, and nothing reminds me of the four continents still owed from 0:43.

Frames 0-90 are identical except for the pulsing '?', motion is 0.10-0.35/s, and the frame is dark. Thumbnail B's composition (flat map, red tips, arrows into the '?') only appears with the flat-map drips at 0:08-0:16. So the first frames neither move nor match the packaging, and the 0:30 intro metric is decided here.
drop_risks.fix: Open mid-spin: rotate the globe about 180 degrees and ease it onto the South America/Africa view by 0:02.5, with the existing drip lines from 0:03-0:16 starting at frame 1. Better: open on the 0:16 flat-map drip frame (thumbnail B in motion) for about 2 s, then cut to the globe on 'South America' (0:03.9).

fatigue_points.why: This is the fifth archival page or portrait since 0:58 (Novum Organum, Bacon, two Latin cards, the page pile-up, Forster), at 136-158 wpm, with no new clue since the hook.
Stats pile-up at 178 wpm over the IF RANDOM dot grid and then a nearly static hemisphere globe (4:44-5:06).
7:30-8:00 stacks 16 pops and 11 abrupt motions over dense physics (squashed ball, radioactivity) at 160 wpm. Busy visuals on top of a hard explanation overload the viewer.
Right after the emotional peak (Wegener's death on the ice, 9:10-9:21) comes a technical passage on magnetized stripes and mid-ocean ridges at 152 wpm.

The core explanation (11:12-11:21, 'their pointy ends all sat close to Antarctica') plays over a static polar map whose pointing arrows are a few pixels wide. The most important 8 s are among the stillest pictures.
The Nevada tangent comes straight after the Holden twist: the question is already answered, and the new topic has nothing to do with it.
Florida limestone: a slowly building platform cross-section, with 9 still seconds in the 13:30-14:00 window.
The verdict recap ('So is the drip just a coincidence?') sounds like the wrap-up and reuses earlier icons (compass, dotted lines, an Earth cutaway with an X).
Three closing lines in a row (15:55, 16:03, 16:14) before the teaser.

strengths: Strong, concrete hook copy: a visual metaphor ('melting'), a labelled list of tips, a joke by 0:12 ('dashboard in July'), then the myth and its refutation by 0:28, matching the title. A clear promise follows at 0:31, plus a specific 3-item roadmap of open questions (0:38-0:55). The 1-s Gondwana flash-forward at 0:30.1 is exactly the playbook's 'flash the final reveal'.

Setups and payoffs all connect: Bacon's 'is there a southern continent?' (1:15) pays off at 10:23-10:32; 'Hold on to him' (2:41) at Holden, 11:34-12:38; 'pyramidal' (2:11) at Green, 6:13; 'four continents' (0:43) at 14:52-15:29; the lopsided planet (0:18) at 5:28 and 14:19; 'not an accident' (1:07) at 16:03. Every open question closes.

The myth-busting device works: JUICE CHECK stamps at 1:30 (FALSE) and 9:52 (TRUE), plus punchlines that land on the cut: 'technically, a houseboat' (2:58), 'asked for a refund' (2:08), 'Argentinians' (4:33), 'Sleep tight, kids' (7:12), 'Reminder: you're a mammal' (15:52).

The pyramid chapter (5:57-8:01) is a self-contained mystery with a twist ('real clues, wrong suspect'). Its check-check-check list on a rotating tetrahedron has the highest motion energy in the film (2.14-2.59).

The Wegener death beat (9:03-9:41) uses the film's only deliberate long pauses (1.2 s after 'back.' and after 'died.') and the '1963: 33 YEARS TOO LATE' reveal. It is an emotional peak that earns goodwill for the payoff.
The payoff is well staged: 'THE BIG DRIPS ARE SCARS' appears on the word (11:32.5) with a 1-s pause, and the Holden twist (12:19-12:38) delivers a second payoff after the first.

Transitions carry meaning: a whip down to the South Pole on 'go to the bottom' (3:10.8), a photo-negative flash on 'photographic negatives' (3:20.2), a polaroid flash on 'snapshot' (14:30.9), and the 2026-to-1620 year roll on the Bacon cards (0:55, 16:03).

The ending mechanics are right: a one-word comment prompt naming the four options (15:29), a callback, the film-strip 'one frame of a very slow movie', a concrete next-story cliffhanger (the Afar Y, 16:19), and the end screen over a still-moving map (16:35-16:51).
The subscribe ask is placed as the playbook says: 34% in, after a payoff, inside an open loop, and it names what the channel offers.
top3: 1. Fix the first 3 seconds and the black at 0:53. These are animation/edit defects and the single biggest lever. Make the globe spin from frame 1 and start the drips immediately, ideally opening on the 0:16 flat-map drip frame, which is thumbnail B in motion. Replace the 1.45 s of black at 0:53.1-0:54.55 with the 4-model grid dimming under the '+250 MILLION YEARS' counter (the asset from 14:44). These two moments set the 0:30 and 1:00 numbers that everything else scales from; expect about +3-5 points at 0:30.

2. Cut the two lecture stretches, with no new narration. Early: cut 1:39-2:11 (Bacon recap and Forster), 4:44-4:50 and 5:06-5:12 (stats), so the first payoff arrives about 45 s sooner. Late: cut Nevada (12:38-12:55.9) and Florida (13:27-13:46), keep the 15-s verdict (14:04-14:19), and move the 'lopsided planet... snapshot' lines (14:19-14:35) into the 15:55-16:03 slot. That removes the false ending, so 'the honest part' runs straight into 'So where is the drip going?'. Expect the 12:00-15:00 loss to shrink from about 6 to about 3-4 points, and more viewers to reach the comment prompt and end screen.

3. Re-render the animation defects, most visible first: the four grid snaps at 15:02.2, 15:11.3, 15:19.9 and 15:29.3 (ease over 12-18 frames or cross-dissolve); the double rewind counter at 10:00-10:13 (remove the number from the flat-map slider), plus the 38-to-180 counter at 11:12.5; the globe brightness pop at 5:45.0 (render-chunk seam 22 to 23, frames 10350-10351); the black matte square behind the Pacific inset at 5:32.3-5:34.6; the empty navy frame at 12:55.9-12:57.1; the 0.5-s calendar flicker at 15:42.5; the 6-frame shake at 10:34.33; and the kids popping in and snapping poses at 7:08 and 7:11.9.
